en.name: Kirimochi (packaged rice cakes)
en.summary: Individually wrapped kirimochi has no general shelf-life figure — the honest answer is the printed date, because the sealed wrapper and its oxygen absorber are the whole preservation system. Once a piece is unwrapped it behaves like fresh mochi and will mould; freeze it instead, for about 6 months.
en.pantry: Store the unopened pack cool, dark and dry, and go by the printed date rather than by any general rule. That is not evasion: each little sachet is sealed with an oxygen absorber, and that seal is what keeps the mochi stable — which is why unopened kirimochi is recommended as a household stockpile food. Inspect the individual packets, not just the outer bag. A sachet that is punctured, puffed up, or whose absorber has been disturbed is finished, whatever the date says.
en.fridge: The refrigerator does not extend the life of an unopened sachet, and for an opened piece it only delays the inevitable: once unwrapped, kirimochi is fresh mochi and will grow mould, often green or pink, starting at the cut faces. Either cook it now or freeze it. The traditional 水餅 method also works for opened pieces — keep them fully submerged in cold water in the fridge and change the water every day — but it is a way of buying a little time, not a way of storing them.
en.freezer: About 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Wrap opened pieces individually in cling film and bag them, so they do not fuse into a slab and do not pick up freezer smells. Let a piece rest briefly at room temperature before grilling or boiling, and cook it from there — the outside will scorch before the centre softens if you take it straight from the freezer to a hot grill.
en.thawing: Let frozen pieces stand a short while at room temperature, then grill, toast or boil them. There is no need to thaw them through, and they should never be left out to thaw for hours.
spoilage: Green, black or pink mould, usually starting at the cut edges.
A punctured or inflated sachet, or one whose seal has clearly failed.
A sour, fermented or musty smell when the wrapper is opened.
Slimy or sticky surface on a piece that should be dry and firm.
tips: Check each individual sachet, not just the outer bag.
Freeze opened pieces the same day rather than leaving them wrapped in the packet.
Wrap individually before freezing so pieces come apart easily.
If you use the water method, change the water daily and keep the container in the fridge.

faq.a: Follow the date printed on the pack. The sealed sachet and its oxygen absorber are the preservation system, and no separate general figure is published.
Yes, about 6 months at −18 °C. That figure is read across from cooked rice rather than published for mochi. Wrap pieces individually first.

faq.q: Can opened mochi be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: Only briefly, and it will still mould. Cook it or freeze it. The traditional method of keeping it submerged in water, changed daily, buys a little extra time.

zh.name: 切り餅（日式年糕塊）
zh.summary: 單片包裝的切り餅沒有通用的保存期限數字——誠實的答案是「看包裝上印的日期」，因為密封袋與裡面的脫氧劑就是它全部的保存系統。一旦拆開，它就是新鮮麻糬，會長霉；這時候該做的是冷凍，大約 6 個月。
zh.pantry: 未開封的整包放陰涼、避光、乾燥處，並以包裝上印的日期為準，而不是套用什麼通則。這不是迴避：每一小片都是連同脫氧劑一起密封的，維持穩定的正是那層密封——這也是為什麼未開封的切り餅會被列為家庭常備儲糧。請檢查每一小包，而不只是外袋。小包破了、鼓起來，或脫氧劑明顯失效的，不管日期怎麼寫都算報廢。
zh.fridge: 冷藏並不會延長未開封小包的壽命；對拆開的餅來說，它也只是拖延而已：一旦拆封，切り餅就是新鮮麻糬，會從切面開始長霉，常見綠色或粉紅色。所以請不是現在煮，就是拿去冷凍。傳統的「水餅」做法對拆開的餅也適用——完全泡在冷水裡放冰箱，每天換水——但那是爭取一點時間，不是保存方式。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下大約 6 個月。拆開的餅請一片一片用保鮮膜包好再裝袋，才不會黏成一大塊，也不會吸冷凍庫的味道。烤或煮之前讓它在室溫稍微回一下再下鍋；直接從冷凍丟進大火烤網，外面焦了裡面還是硬的。
zh.thawing: 冷凍的餅在室溫稍微放一下，就可以直接烤、煎或煮，不需要完全解凍，也絕對不要放在室溫退冰好幾個小時。
spoilage: 長出綠色、黑色或粉紅色的霉，通常從切面開始。
小包破孔或鼓脹，或密封明顯失效。
拆開時聞到酸味、發酵味或霉味。
本該乾爽結實的表面變得黏滑。
tips: 要逐片檢查小包，不要只看外袋。
拆開的餅當天就冷凍，不要包回袋子裡放著。
冷凍前一片片單獨包好，之後才拆得開。
用水餅法就要每天換水，而且容器要放冰箱。

faq.a: 以包裝上印的日期為準。密封小包與脫氧劑就是保存系統，並沒有另外公布的通用數字。
可以，−18 °C 下大約 6 個月。這個數字是比照熟米飯得來的，不是為麻糬公布的。冷凍前請一片片包好。

faq.q: 拆開的麻糬可以冰冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 只能放很短，而且還是會長霉。請煮掉或冷凍。傳統泡水、每天換水的做法可以多爭取一點時間。
